source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: The pdf file mentions some kind of level sifter, but I don't understand what it is for

ambiguity.description: It is unclear whether the sensor-board level-shifter provision is required and what sensor behavior it is intended to support.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The level shifter was listed as DNP (Do Not Populate) by default — just the footprint on the PCB without components soldered. The purpose was future-proofing: if someone later connects a 5V-logic sensor to the spare I2C0 or UART connectors, they could populate the BSS138s to make it work. Since all sensors in our current BOM work at 3.3V (including SPS30 and ZE08 which are 5V-powered but 3.3V logic compatible), the level shifter is not needed for any connected sensor. You can skip it entirely to save board space. If we ever need 5V-logic sensors later, we'll add a small adapter board rather than reserving permanent footprints.
